THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Dan-O's Bone-In Chicken Thighs

Two trays. Two seasonings. One oven. Adults get Dan-O's Spicy, kids get Dan-O's Original. Same cook, different plates — that's the whole brand in one dinner.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME45 min (5 min hands-on)
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~480 cal | ~38g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: PAT DRY hard. Paper towels, both sides, every thigh. Wet skin = rubber skin.

Ingredients

PROTEIN

  • 8 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs (~4-5 oz each)
  • 1-2 tbsp avocado or olive oil (just enough to coat)
  • Pinch of salt (Dan-O's is salted, but a small assist helps)

ADULT FINISH

  • 1-2 tbsp Umami Lemon Heat Sauce (drizzle over asparagus)
  • Cracked black pepper

Option 2

  • Dan-O's Original Seasoning (heavy coat — both sides)
  • 1 small flour tortilla per kid (cut in half), warmed

VEG (shared base)

  • 1 large bunch asparagus (1-1.5 lbs), trimmed
  • Olive oil + salt + pepper

ADULT TRAY

  • Dan-O's Spicy Seasoning (heavy coat — both sides)

Option 1

  • Dan-O's Original Seasoning (heavy coat — both sides)
  • 1 small flour tortilla per kid (cut in half), warmed

Allergens: mustard.

AT THE PAN. Two trays, two seasonings. Adult tray = Dan-O's Spicy. Kid tray = Dan-O's Original. Bake on the same rack, same time, same temp. Zero workflow split.

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.PREHEAT. Oven to 425°F. Convection if you have it.
  2. 2.PAT DRY. Paper towels, every thigh, both sides. Press hard. This is the most important step.
  3. 3.OIL. Drizzle oil, rub it in. Tiny pinch of salt on each thigh.
  4. 4.ASPARAGUS PREP. Snap off woody ends. Toss with olive oil, salt, pepper. Single layer on a sheet pan.

Adult — Dan-O's Spicy + Umami Lemon Heat Drizzle

  1. 5.SEASON. Coat both sides of the adult thighs HEAVY with Dan-O's Spicy. You should barely see the chicken.
  2. 6.BAKE. Skin-side up on the adult tray. 425°F, 35-40 min. Don't flip, don't open the oven before 30.
  3. 7.ASPARAGUS. Roast the same time, same oven. 12-15 min until tender + slightly charred. Pull when thighs are at 30 min mark.
  4. 8.MAKE THE SAUCE. 3 minutes — mayo + lemon + soy + Dijon + chili oil. Whisk smooth, rest 5 min. (See Umami Lemon Heat Sauce in Cookbook.)
  5. 9.PLATE. 2 thighs over charred asparagus, drizzle Umami Lemon Heat over the asparagus. Crack of pepper. Done.

Kid — Dan-O's Original + Plain Asparagus + Wrap · Option 1

  1. 5.SEASON. Coat both sides of kid thighs with Dan-O's Original. Same heavy hand — Original isn't spicy, just savory.
  2. 6.BAKE. Same rack as adult tray, 425°F, 35-40 min.
  3. 7.WRAP. Warm tortilla in microwave 15 sec or on a dry pan. Cut in half, fold.
  4. 8.PLATE. 1 thigh + plain asparagus (no tapenade) + folded wrap. Mild, familiar, no resistance.

Kid — Dan-O's Original + Plain Asparagus + Wrap · Option 2

  1. 5.SAME COOK. Just plate the thigh + the warm folded wrap. No fight over asparagus.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — Dan-O's Spicy + Umami Lemon Heat Drizzle: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid — Dan-O's Original + Plain Asparagus + Wrap: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • Two trays. Don't try to do half-and-half in one pan — the seasonings will cross.
  • Coat aggressively. You should not see chicken skin under the seasoning.

If something fails

Skin is rubbery / soft: You didn't pat dry enough, OR oven temp was too low. 425°F minimum. Wet skin can't crisp.

Tastes bland: Under-seasoned. Dan-O's needs a heavy hand — you should barely see chicken under the coating. Add a pinch of salt on top of the seasoning if needed.

Meat is dry: Used boneless skinless. Use BONE-IN SKIN-ON. The bone retains heat, the skin protects the meat. Non-negotiable.

Seasoning burnt: Oven too hot or thighs too small. 425°F is the cap. If thighs are tiny, pull at 30 min.

Kids won't eat the wrap side: Skip it. The thigh is the meal. Wrap is just a comfort carb if they're hungry.

Storage and reheating

Store: Cooked thighs in an airtight container, fridge. Pour the rendered pan juices over the chicken before sealing — that's the secret weapon for next-day tacos.

Reheat: Air fryer 350°F for 4-5 min — re-crisps the skin. Don't microwave (turns skin rubbery).

Lasts: 3-4 days in fridge. Skin loses some crispness but flavor holds.

Estimated nutrition

~480 cal | ~38g protein.

Filmed one-pan version: two family dinners

The new video shows a different cook from the original two-tray, 425°F recipe above. Both mild and spicy bone-in thighs shared one pan. Adults got Umami Lemon Heat on asparagus; the first-night kid plate had plain asparagus and a buttered bun. The second-night kid plate was not filmed.

What the filmed batch used

  • •Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs; filmed portions were not weighed
  • •Dan-O's Original for the kid side and Dan-O's Spicy for the adult side
  • •Asparagus for both plates; a buttered bun for the filmed first-night kid plate
  • •Umami Lemon Heat adult finish: light mayonnaise, lemon, soy sauce, Dijon, and chili oil
  • •Reserved pan juices for storing and reheating the chicken

How the filmed version came together

  1. 1Pat the thighs dry. Arrange in one pan, keeping the Original-seasoned kid pieces separate from the Spicy adult pieces.
  2. 2Roast uncovered. This filmed pan took about 90 minutes at 350°F; thigh size and oven conditions vary. Use a thermometer to verify 165°F in the thickest part, away from the bone.
  3. 3Cook asparagus. Whisk light mayonnaise, lemon, soy, Dijon, and chili oil for the adult Umami Lemon Heat finish. Keep the kid asparagus plain.
  4. 4Serve adults chicken with sauced asparagus. Serve the first-night kid plate with plain asparagus and a buttered bun. Save remaining chicken with its pan juices; refrigerate promptly.
  5. 5For dinner two, reheat the refrigerated chicken with its juices. The filmed reheat took about 30 minutes at 350°F; use a thermometer to check the center reaches 165°F before serving.
Filmed-batch nutrition

The adult ~48g protein and kid ~28g protein values elsewhere on this page are estimates from the original recipe portions. The filmed portions were not weighed, so no measured nutrition total is claimed for the one-pan version.
